description: Strontium is a chemical element with symbol Sr and atomic number 38, and is an alkaline earth metal. It is a soft silver-white yellowish metallic element that is highly chemically reactive and forms a dark oxide layer when exposed to air. It has physical and chemical properties similar to calcium and barium, occurring naturally mainly in the minerals celestine and strontianite.
uses: During the 19th century, strontium was mostly used in the production of sugar from sugar beets. At the peak of television cathode-ray tube production, as much as 75% of strontium consumption in the United States was used for the faceplate glass. Volatile strontium salts are used in pyrotechnics and in the production of flares, and the isotope 89Sr is used to treat bone cancer.
characteristics: Strontium is a divalent silvery metal with a pale yellow tint, softer than calcium and harder than barium. Its melting point is 777 °C and boiling point is 1377 °C, with a density of 2.64 g/cm³. It is intermediate in reactivity between calcium and barium, and finely powdered strontium metal is pyrophoric, meaning it will ignite spontaneously in air at room temperature.
